text:
deploy-bot: ALERT: service=edge-ingress | 7/10 targets unhealthy, 3 deregistered. failing check: ALB healthcheck returns HTTP 421 on TLS probe.

alex: seeing the same in ALB logs — a bunch of 421s around 10:25 UTC. odd one, not 502/504.

maria: FYI we rolled a transit/inspection route at 10:22 as part of the egress inspection rollout (TGW->inspection). could be related.

samir: 421 Misdirected Request usually means HTTP/2 connection was reused for a different origin (host/SNI mismatch). if the inspection appliance is proxying TLS and reusing connections it might trigger this.

jin: i reproduced from an edge node with curl. output: 
```
$ curl -v -H 'Host: edge.prod.internal' https://10.2.5.12:8443/health
* Connected to 10.2.5.12 (10.2.5.12) port 8443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: edge.prod.internal
> User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 421 Misdirected Request
< content-length: 18
< content-type: text/plain

misdirected request
```

alex: app logs show healthchecks arriving with different Host headers (edge.staging) which we never set for the ALB check. so the host header is getting altered somewhere.

maria: ALB uses SNI + Host header to route to the right virtualhost in our sidecar. if the inspection device terminates TLS and re-issues client TLS, it may not preserve original SNI/Host mapping or it may multiplex connections across hosts. that would explain 421.

samir: pulled VPC flow + inspection logs — healthcheck traffic for ALB egress is hitting the inspection appliance and it's set to HTTP/2 proxy with connection pooling. it looks like it's reusing backend connections across different SNI values.

jin: quick mitigation options: change healthcheck to plain HTTP (no TLS) on a dedicated port/path that ignores Host, or set the ALB healthcheck to include an explicit Host header that our proxy preserves, or use NLB/TCP check.

alex: can we switch to a hostless health endpoint (eg /hc-no-vhost) that returns 200 regardless of Host?

maria: yes — we have that endpoint on each edge pod already but the target group uses TLS health probe. changing to HTTP health check on port 8080 with path /hc-no-vhost should be fast.

samir: i'll apply the change to the target group now as a temp mitigation. will also open a ticket with the inspection team to disable connection pooling for proxied healthchecks.

deploy-bot: deploy 2445006789/infra: modified target-group health check -> HTTP on port 8080 path /hc-no-vhost (host override removed).

jin: after change, targets are coming back: 10/10 healthy, no more 421s in last 2 minutes.

maria: created SEC-4821 for inspection team to preserve SNI + Host for ALB healthcheck flows and to add explicit bypass for health probes. added runbook step to prefer hostless health endpoints when an inspection appliance is in-path.

alex: note added to runbook: "If TGW/inspection is enabled, prefer non-vhost healthchecks or use NLB/TCP checks."

samir: following up with diagram and PR to infra-templates to default to /hc-no-vhost for edge target groups behind inspection. will also audit other services. :thumbsup:

jin: long-term we should either ensure inspection proxies preserve SNI/Host or move healthchecks off TLS paths. next action: coordination with security/inspection team to change proxy behavior.

maria: thanks team, great catch. closing incident once we've validated no regression after 1h. :white_check_mark:
